stem:
When pure water is saturated with both CaCO3 and CaC2O4, the
concentration of calcium ion in the solution under equilibrium is 8 ×
10-5 M. If the ratio of the solubility product of CaCO3 to that of
CaC2O4 is 3, what is the solubility product of CaCO3 in pure water ?
Report your answer after multiplying by 109 and rounding it off to
nearest whole number.
solution:
${CaCO}_{3} \rightleftharpoons {Ca}^{+ 2} + {CO}_{3}^{- 2}$
${CaC}_{2}O_{4} \ \ \rightleftharpoons \ {Ca}^{+ 2} + \ C_{2}O_{4}^{- 2}$
x x y y
(x+y) x (x+y) y
$\frac{K_{SP}\left( {CaCO}_{3} \right)}{K_{SP}\left( {CaC}_{2}O_{4} \right)} = \frac{x}{y} = 3 \Rightarrow x = 3y$
$(x + y) = 8 \times 10^{- 5}$
$(3y + y) = 8 \times 10^{- 5}$
$\Rightarrow y = 2 \times 10^{- 5}x = 6 \times 10^{- 5}$
$K_{SP}\left( {CaCO}_{3} \right) = \left\lbrack {Ca}^{+ 2} \right\rbrack\left\lbrack {CO}_{3}^{- 2} \right\rbrack$
$= 8 \times 10^{- 5} \times 6 \times 10^{- 5}$
$= 48 \times 10^{- 10}$
$K_{SP}\left( {CaCO}_{3} \right) = 4.8 \times 10^{- 9}$

$HX = H^{+} + X^{-}$

$\therefore K_{a} \times K_{b} = \lbrack H^{+}\rbrack\lbrack OH^{-}\rbrack = K_{v} = 10^{- 14}$

Now as $\lbrack X^{-}\rbrack = \lbrack HX\rbrack,pH = pK_{a} = 4$
